rationale_bullets: All three 2025 QBs left a 5th-pctile passing offense; Alonza Barnett III arrives as the 2025 Sun Belt POY: 2,806 (58%, 23-8) plus 589 rushing and 15 rush TD (6th among QBs), 21-6 as a starter, a CFP appearance - 'a winner to build the 2026 team around' (P6).
The dual-threat fit with Frost's scheme is the consensus story across all three books; his late-'24 ACL is now two seasons back.
The tape tempers the hardware: PFF 71.1/433 and a 58% completion rate - good, not elite, and Sun Belt-graded (G5 guard).
Jenkins (33 FIU starts, 6,713 career) is a proven backup; 4* Marriott is the program's highest-rated QB commit. 52 = average-plus.
grades_detail.g5_guard_note: SBC POY production graded with the level discount; fit + winner profile hold it above average

rationale_bullets: Both producers left for the pros (Montgomery 76.9; 705 workhorse yards; Nixon 69.9; 554 explosive) and Gage followed to LSU.
The reload is talent-over-proof: Watson (64.5; led the FBS at 8.9 ypc in '24 but injury-marked, 755 career yards), Chambers (1,273 at 5.2 - FCS), Swint (PS#26 pedigree, zero tape after the redshirt).
'25's 48th-pctile RUN grade came 'in spite of the line' (#29 ypc vs #95 Run Push) - the room profile stays explosive, but nobody has carried an FBS load. 46 = fringe-below-average.
grades_detail.g5_guard_note: Chambers' 1,273 is FCS-graded; Watson's ypc is 41-carry-sample '24

rationale_bullets: The retained core is real: Thomas (69.0; 53/528 used everywhere), TE Wade (68.5; 43/523/5 - every program TE record, All-B12 HM, a must-retain), Charles (59.1; 26/290 as a true FR with 'highlight reel' framing).
Additions bring resumes, not P4 tape: Derry (Monmouth 1st-team FCS AA; 1,123 at 14.8), Bibbs (70.3; 383 at ULM); Farmer returns from the missed season.
'25 RECV was 10th pctile - but it was fed by a broken QB room; PS: 'much more experienced and should top the last two years production.'
48 = fringe-average: quality retained pieces, no proven P4 No. 1.
grades_detail.g5_guard_note: Derry's AA season is FCS-graded; the 48 leans on the returning P4 trio

rationale_bullets: One returning starter (Cushman 63.1/753) plus Meadows' four starts - four '25 starters gone from a line that was 23rd-pctile run-blocking, #95 in P6's Run Push, and 'heavily penalized… often killing drives.'

Four three-star transfers rebuild it: Tabansi (64.6/828; 25 Buffalo starts), Wayburn (71.9/445 UConn - the best incoming tape), Terpstra (MSU; 1 start), Gibson (53.2 Charlotte); 60 incoming career starts.
The interior is unsettled (PS prints Meadows at center, Athlon Terpstra); staff confidence ('improved over last year' - PS) is from a low base.
40 = below average: the second straight transfer-built line protecting a new QB.
The edge pair left for the pros (Lawrence 80.1/470 + Kelly 76.2/492 - 10 of 27 team sacks) and the interior lost Walker (70.7) to Ohio State, LeBlanc to Maryland, Lora to Purdue.
What returns is better than the proxy sees: RJ Jackson (69.3/456; 11 st), Lockett (withdrawal override, triple-sourced - 85.2 on 113 snaps before the week-4 injury), 4* Nixon (62.8) and Edwards.
Dall (79.3/628; All-MAC, 8.5 TFL, 7 pd) is the best incoming tape among seven transfers (Collins 12 OreSt starts, Gurley 10.5 TFL FCS, Talley, Top200 Harrold off a DNP).
PS: 'depth but might be down a notch… looking for more interior pressure'; Athlon: edge is 'the biggest question.' From RDEF 80th/PRSH 71st: 48 = fringe-average.
grades_detail.g5_guard_note: Dall's 79.3 is MAC-graded; Gurley FCS - guard keeps the unit at fringe-average despite depth

rationale_bullets: Carter (75.9/692; team-high 92 tackles, 4th-team B12) was a must-retain and stayed - 'should push for all-league honors again' (P6).

The second level rebuilds with volume: Culbreath (66.4/626; 13 st, 71 tkl, 9 TFL at ODU), Curtis (63.3/321; Wisconsin 4*, 40 tackles as a USC freshman), Henry (67 tkl at UMass); Jennings (70.3/135) returns.
Kozlowski (75.6/531; #2 tackler) graduated. PS: 'this unit is smart and really packs a punch.' 52 = average-plus around one proven star.

Four of five starters return from a 75th-pctile coverage unit: Bellamy (76.4/666; 4th-team B12, 8 pbu - 'the top corner'), A.Jackson (66.8/557; 5 pbu), Marshall (64.5/476; 2 INT, must-retain), Henderson (71.0/700; 61 tkl).
The lone loss is real - Dunnam (75.3/781, #3 tackler) - and the open safety is a battle: J.Williams (68.1), Bartrum (Harvard 3rd-team FCS AA; 83 tkl), Wayne St's 12-pd Johnson, Flagg.
PS: 'maybe they can climb to that '23 [#16 PDR] level… a solid defensive backfield'; Athlon calls the secondary the strength. 58 = the roster's most proven unit.
The punter is proven: Bertrams (Wisconsin; 45.3 avg/40.1 net in '24, PS#25) - a real upgrade path; ST coordinator Alamar is retained after lifting the unit #108 -> #73.
The placekicker is not: Stone (Texas) is a kickoff specialist (98 KO/56 TB in '24) who 'has never attempted a field goal in a college game' (Athlon's explicit flag); K Ruelas (15-17, L54) is gone.
KR Nixon (the KR-TD) also departs (FR Kaj Baker takes over). From a 76th-pctile SPEC season: 45 = fringe-below-average - the FG void is the swing risk PS's 'wont drop much' underweights.
